hints: Show that two adjacent sides are perpendicular by evaluating their scalar product: $\vec{OA} \cdot \vec{OC} = 0$.
Show that opposite sides are equal vectors: $\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA} = \vec{OC}$.
Conclude that a parallelogram with a right angle is a rectangle.
walkthrough:
Write the position vectors in column vector form:
$$\vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 2 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{OC} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the scalar product of the adjacent sides $\vec{OA}$ and $\vec{OC}$:
$$\vec{OA} \cdot \vec{OC} = (5)(3) + (-2)(4) + (1)(-7) = 15 - 8 - 7 = 0$$
Since the scalar product is zero, $\vec{OA}$ and $\vec{OC}$ are perpendicular, so $\angle AOC = 90^\circ$.

Find the displacement vector $\vec{AB}$ from $A$ to $B$:
$$\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 2 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 - 5 \\ 2 - (-2) \\ -6 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compare $\vec{AB}$ with $\vec{OC}$:
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix} = \vec{OC}$$
Since $\vec{AB} = \vec{OC}$, the opposite sides $AB$ and $OC$ are parallel and have equal length.

Conclude the geometric proof:
A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram. Since the adjacent sides $OA$ and $OC$ meet at a right angle, $OABC$ is a rectangle.

hints: Find the vectors representing the diagonals $\vec{OB}$ and $\vec{AC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OA}$.
Compute the magnitudes $|\vec{OB}|$ and $|\vec{AC}|$, then apply $\cos\theta = \dfrac{|\vec{OB} \cdot \vec{AC}|}{|\vec{OB}||\vec{AC}|}$.
walkthrough:
Identify the vectors representing the two diagonals of the rectangle:
$$\text{Diagonal 1: } \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 2 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\text{Diagonal 2: } \vec{AC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 5 \\ 4 - (-2) \\ -7 - 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 6 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix}$$

Apply the scalar product angle formula to find the acute angle $\theta$ between the diagonals:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{|\vec{OB} \cdot \vec{AC}|}{|\vec{OB}||\vec{AC}|} = \dfrac{44}{\sqrt{104}\sqrt{104}} = \dfrac{44}{104}$$

Simplify the fraction and evaluate the angle in degrees and radians:
$$\dfrac{44}{104} = \dfrac{11}{26} \approx 0.4230769$$
$$\theta = \arccos\left(\dfrac{11}{26}\right) \approx 64.974^\circ \approx 65.0^\circ \quad (\text{or } 1.13 \text{ radians})$$
